topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Under 12-10-204(1), which of the following is NOT required to maintain errors and omissions insurance to cover activities under Part 2?
choice_a: An inactive broker, or an attorney licensee who maintains a policy of professional malpractice insurance covering their activities as a licensee
choice_b: An active broker who works independently
choice_c: A broker who has been licensed for less than one year
choice_d: A broker employed by a brokerage firm with more than one broker
explanation: 12-10-204(1) exempts 'an inactive broker or an attorney licensee who maintains a policy of professional malpractice insurance that provides coverage for errors and omissions for their activities as a licensee under this part 2' from the E&O requirement.

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: How does the division make errors and omissions insurance available to all licensees under 12-10-204?
choice_a: By requiring each licensee to independently shop for the lowest-cost carrier
choice_b: By contracting with an insurer for a group policy after a competitive bid process
choice_c: By self-insuring licensees directly through the Commission
choice_d: By reimbursing licensees for individually purchased premiums
explanation: The statute states the division 'shall make the errors and omissions insurance available to all licensees by contracting with an insurer for a group policy after a competitive bid process in accordance with article 103 of title 24.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Under the group errors and omissions policy obtained by the division, what right does the insurer have to cancel an individual licensee's coverage?
choice_a: The insurer may cancel a licensee for nonpayment only
choice_b: The insurer may cancel a licensee with 30 days' written notice
choice_c: The insurer has no right to cancel a licensee
choice_d: The insurer may cancel a licensee whenever a claim is filed against them
explanation: The text states the group policy 'must be available to all licensees with no right on the part of the insurer to cancel a licensee.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: If the division is unable to obtain group E&O coverage for all participating licensees at a reasonable annual premium, what must a licensee do?
choice_a: Wait for the division to renegotiate before practicing
choice_b: Request a fee waiver from the Commission
choice_c: Operate without E&O insurance until the next renewal date
choice_d: Independently obtain the required errors and omissions insurance
explanation: 12-10-204(2)(a) provides that if the division cannot obtain coverage for all licensees at a reasonable premium, 'a licensee shall independently obtain the errors and omissions insurance required by this section.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: How far in advance of the annual premium renewal date must the Commission notify each licensee of the required E&O terms and conditions?
choice_a: At least thirty days before the annual premium renewal date
choice_b: At least fifteen days before the annual premium renewal date
choice_c: At least sixty days before the annual premium renewal date
choice_d: At least ten days before the annual premium renewal date
explanation: 12-10-204(3) requires the Commission to 'notify each licensee of the required terms and conditions at least thirty days before the annual premium renewal date as determined by the commission.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per 12-10-205, in addition to the licensee's name, what must appear imprinted on a Colorado real estate license?
choice_a: The licensee's photograph
choice_b: The seal, or a facsimile, of the department
choice_c: The licensee's fingerprint classification number
choice_d: The name of the licensee's E&O insurance carrier
explanation: 12-10-205 states the license 'shall show the name of the licensee and shall have imprinted thereon the seal, or a facsimile, of the department.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: A nonresident applicant wants to become a Colorado real estate broker but maintains a definite place of business in their home state. Per 12-10-208(1), what does this mean for the Colorado business-location requirement?
choice_a: They must still maintain a place of business in Colorado
choice_b: They must appoint a Colorado resident as co-broker
choice_c: They are not required to maintain a place of business within Colorado
choice_d: They may not conduct business in Colorado at all
explanation: 12-10-208(1) provides that a nonresident broker 'shall not be required to maintain a place of business within this state if that broker maintains a definite place of business in another state.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: A broker has no locatable registered agent and is served by certified mail, return receipt requested. If the return receipt is never signed and the broker never otherwise receives the process, when is service perfected?
choice_a: Immediately upon mailing
choice_b: Ten days after mailing
choice_c: Thirty days after mailing
choice_d: Five days after mailing
explanation: 12-10-208(2) lists service as perfected at the earliest of receipt by the broker, the date on a signed return receipt, or 'five days after mailing' -- so absent the first two, the five-day mark governs.

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.1.A, an applicant for an Initial License must submit a set of fingerprints to which agency?
choice_a: The Colorado Bureau of Investigation
choice_b: The Federal Bureau of Investigation
choice_c: The Colorado Division of Insurance
choice_d: The Colorado Real Estate Commission
explanation: Rule 3.1.A.3 requires an applicant to 'submit a set of fingerprints to the Colorado Bureau of Investigation as set forth in Rule 2.3.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.1.A, when must an applicant for an Initial License acquire errors and omissions insurance?
choice_a: Only after passing the licensing exam but before submitting fingerprints
choice_b: Prior to obtaining an Active License
choice_c: Within one year of initial licensure
choice_d: Only if applying at the Broker (not Associate Broker) level
explanation: Rule 3.1.A.4 requires an applicant to 'acquire errors and omissions insurance as set forth in Rule 3.9. prior to obtaining an Active License.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.2, if an application is canceled because the accompanying payment was invalid (e.g., a bounced check), within how many days of the Division's notification of the incomplete application may the applicant seek reinstatement, with full payment of Fees plus the reinstatement clerical fee?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 15 days
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 60 days
explanation: Rule 3.2 allows reinstatement 'only at the discretion of the Commission and upon full payment of any Fees together with payment of the fee required...within thirty (30) days of the Division's notification of an incomplete application.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.3, if the Division deems an application incomplete, how long does the applicant have to provide the missing documentation before the application is canceled and the Fee forfeited?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 20 days
choice_c: 45 days
choice_d: 30 days
explanation: Rule 3.3 states an applicant notified of deficiencies 'will have thirty (30) days to provide the documentation; otherwise, the application will be canceled and the Fee will be forfeited.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.4.A.1, the court case disposition or registry of action submitted by an applicant with a criminal history must include each of the following EXCEPT:
choice_a: The victim's name and contact information
choice_b: The offense(s) convicted of and the statute(s) or municipal code(s) violated
choice_c: The date of conviction and the date of sentencing
choice_d: The status of the case, including current compliance with sentencing/probation terms if not yet completed
explanation: Rule 3.4.A.1 lists offense, statute/code violated, classification, date of conviction, date of sentencing, sentencing terms, and status of case as required elements; no victim information is listed among them.

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.4.A.4, if an applicant with a criminal record is applying for an Active License, the Employing Broker's signed statement must specify which level of supervision the Employing Broker feels is appropriate?
choice_a: Either Direct or Indirect Supervision
choice_b: Either a Reasonable or a High-Level of Supervision
choice_c: Either Probationary or Standard Supervision
choice_d: Either Full-Time or Part-Time Supervision
explanation: Rule 3.4.A.4 requires the statement to 'include the level of supervision, either a Reasonable or a High-Level of Supervision, that the Employing Broker feels is appropriate based upon the Applicant's violation(s).'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.4.B, which item is listed as SUPPLEMENTAL (not required) documentation an applicant with a criminal record may submit to demonstrate rehabilitation, truthfulness, honesty, and good moral character?
choice_a: Police officer's arrest report
choice_b: Court case disposition or registry of action
choice_c: Employment history for the preceding five years
choice_d: Signed written explanation of the circumstances of each violation
explanation: Rule 3.4.B.1 lists 'Employment history for the preceding five (5) years' under Supplemental Documentation, distinct from the Required Documentation listed under Rule 3.4.A.

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.5, an applicant with a past or pending professional disciplinary action must submit relevant available documentation, which may include each of the following EXCEPT:
choice_a: Any final agency order(s)
choice_b: Any consent order(s) or stipulation(s)
choice_c: Any investigative report(s)
choice_d: A notarized letter from the disciplining agency's director
explanation: Rule 3.5 lists final agency orders, consent orders, stipulations, investigative reports, and a signed written explanation from the applicant -- it does not require a notarized letter from the disciplining agency's director.

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.6.B, once an application is deemed complete and not subject to further review under Rules 3.4 and 3.5, within how many business days after review of satisfactory fingerprint-based criminal history results will the Commission issue a License?
choice_a: 10 business days
choice_b: 5 business days
choice_c: 15 business days
choice_d: 20 business days
explanation: Rule 3.6.B states the Commission 'will issue a License within ten (10) business days after review of satisfactory results from the fingerprint-based criminal history record check, if applicable.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.6.C, an Initial License issued to an applicant who has successfully satisfied the licensure requirements expires on what date?
choice_a: The anniversary date of issuance
choice_b: December 31 of the year of issuance
choice_c: June 30 of the following year
choice_d: Two years from the date of issuance
explanation: Rule 3.6.C states each qualifying applicant 'will be issued an Initial License expiring December 31 of the year of issuance.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.6.E, a broker's application has been approved subject to receipt of E&O insurance proof and identification of an Employing Broker for supervision. If that proof is not submitted within 30 days after written notification by the Commission, what happens?
choice_a: The application is automatically canceled and the fee forfeited
choice_b: The Applicant must reapply from the beginning
choice_c: The License will be issued on an Inactive status
choice_d: The Commission will deny the License outright
explanation: Rule 3.6.E states such a License 'will be issued on an Inactive status if such proof is not submitted within thirty (30) days after written notification by the Commission.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.6.F, under what circumstance may the Commission refuse to issue a License to a partnership, limited liability company, or corporation?
choice_a: If the entity has fewer than three members
choice_b: If the entity was formed less than one year ago
choice_c: If the entity's registered agent resides out of state
choice_d: If the entity's name is the same as, or so similar as to be easily confused with, that of a person or entity whose License has been suspended or revoked
explanation: Rule 3.6.F allows refusal to issue a License to such an entity if its name 'is the same as that of any person or entity whose License has been suspended or revoked or is so similar as to be easily confused with that of the suspended or revoked person or entity by members of the general public.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.7.B, if the Commission denies an application for licensure, what is the Commission required to do?
choice_a: Inform the Applicant of the denial and the reasons for the denial in writing
choice_b: Provide no explanation at all
choice_c: Give only a verbal explanation at a hearing
choice_d: Automatically refer the Applicant to legal counsel
explanation: Rule 3.7.B states that if an applicant is denied, 'the Applicant will be informed of the denial and the reasons for the denial in writing.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.8, a preliminary advisory opinion issued by the Commission regarding the effect of past criminal or disciplinary history on a future licensure application is:
choice_a: Binding on the Commission and appealable
choice_b: Not binding on the Commission and not appealable
choice_c: Binding only if the opinion is favorable
choice_d: Automatically incorporated into any future formal application without further review
explanation: Rule 3.8 states the Commission 'may, at its sole discretion, issue an opinion which will not be binding on the Commission; is not appealable; and will not limit the authority of the Commission to investigate a future application for licensure.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.9.B, the Commission Insurance Policy must provide, at minimum, what per-claim and annual aggregate coverage per licensed person/entity (not including investigation and defense costs)?
choice_a: $50,000 per claim / $150,000 aggregate
choice_b: $250,000 per claim / $500,000 aggregate
choice_c: $100,000 per claim / $300,000 aggregate
choice_d: $1,000,000 per claim / $1,000,000 aggregate
explanation: Rule 3.9.B.4-5 requires 'Not less than one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) coverage for each licensed person and entity per covered claim' and 'An annual aggregate limit of not less than three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) per licensed Broker or Brokerage Firm.'

topic: License Issuance, Application Review, and Errors & Omissions Insurance
question: Per Rule 3.9.B.9, the Commission Insurance Policy must include coverage for a broker's use of lock boxes of not less than what amount per occurrence?
choice_a: $10,000 per occurrence
choice_b: $50,000 per occurrence
choice_c: $100,000 per occurrence
choice_d: $25,000 per occurrence
explanation: Rule 3.9.B.9 requires 'Coverage of a Broker's use of lock boxes, which coverage must not be less than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) per occurrence.'
